lesson: Advanced small talk & building rapport (B2 · Aula 2)

cards.definition: Light, friendly conversation about unimportant subjects.
cards.example:
- Brazilians are naturally good at small talk, but the rules change across cultures.
Brasileiros são naturalmente bons de small talk, mas as regras mudam entre culturas.

cards.definition: Interests or opinions that two people share.
cards.example:
- We found common ground in five minutes: both of us love trail running.
Encontramos pontos em comum em cinco minutos: nós dois amamos trail running.

cards.definition: A question that cannot be answered with yes or no.
cards.example:
- Open-ended questions keep the conversation flowing without any effort.
Perguntas abertas mantêm a conversa fluindo sem nenhum esforço.
cards.note: O contrário é closed question (resposta sim/não).

cards.example:
- People can always tell when your interest in them is genuine.
As pessoas sempre percebem quando seu interesse por elas é genuíno.

cards.definition: To involve someone actively in a conversation or activity.
cards.example:
- Great hosts engage everyone in the conversation, even the quiet ones.
Bons anfitriões envolvem todo mundo na conversa, até os mais quietos.
cards.note: Engage with someone; cuidado: engaged também significa noivo.

cards.example:
- There was an awkward silence after his joke about the CEO.
Houve um silêncio constrangedor depois da piada dele sobre o CEO.
cards.note: Awkward silence é a colocação clássica.

cards.definition: To say or do something that makes a first conversation easier.
cards.example:
- I always break the ice with a question about the host city.
Eu sempre quebro o gelo com uma pergunta sobre a cidade do evento.
cards.note: Quem quebra o gelo usa um icebreaker.

cards.translation: ter química imediata, se dar bem de cara
cards.example:
- We hit it off immediately and talked for an hour after the meeting ended.
Tivemos química na hora e conversamos por uma hora depois da reunião.
cards.note: We hit it off = a conexão foi instantânea.

cards.definition: A calm exchange of ideas about a subject.
cards.example:
- We had a productive discussion about the new market strategy.
Tivemos uma conversa produtiva sobre a nova estratégia de mercado.
cards.note: “Discussão” (bate-boca) é argument. Discussion é neutro e profissional.

cards.definition: To start again after a pause.
cards.example:
- Let’s resume the conversation after the coffee break.
Vamos retomar a conversa depois do coffee break.
cards.note: “Resumir” é summarize; currículo é résumé ou CV.

exercise.title: Advanced small talk & building rapport (B2 · Aula 2)

questions.explanation: One of the few places where “make” beats “do” outright.

questions.prompt: You both love trail running. You…
questions.explanation: You FIND or HAVE common ground, and it is uncountable — no “a”.
You ASK a question. “Fazer uma pergunta” is the trap behind “make”.

questions.prompt: People can always tell when your interest is _____.
Great hosts _____ everyone in the conversation, even the quiet ones.
questions.explanation: “Engage IN” an activity, “engage WITH” a person.

questions.prompt: There was an _____ silence after his joke about the CEO.
Uma pergunta sobre a viagem dele quebrou o gelo em dez segundos.
questions.answer: A question about his trip broke the ice in ten seconds.|A question about his trip broke the ice in 10 seconds.
questions.explanation: “Break the ice” — the article stays, and the past of “break” is “broke”.

questions.prompt: You liked each other from the first minute. You…
questions.explanation: A fixed phrase: the “it” never changes.

questions.prompt: Which one is a calm exchange of ideas?
questions.explanation: In English a “discussion” is calm; “argument” is the heated one. Portuguese “discussão” is the opposite.

questions.prompt: The meeting stopped for lunch and started again at two. It…
questions.explanation: “Resume” is to continue after a pause. The Portuguese “resumir” is “summarize”.
